name: netdust-agent
description: 0.24.0: the PLAN carries placement and deploy. Reviews, tiers, lanes and batching were already planned; where a dispatch runs was improvised, so gate-check now refuses a cluster with 2+ OPEN [P] tasks and no declared isolation — subagents share the controller working tree, which on 2026-08-09 produced 14 and 17 phantom failures with the rule sitting unread in herdr-moments. A cluster whose [P] tasks are done is never asked. Tasks touching a custom plugin/theme WARN when no ## Deploy block mentions the payload (deploy.payload is a closed list; a missing path deploys as an empty directory a rollback deletes) — a warn, not a fail, because is-this-new is a guess. PLACEMENT. Dispatch answers what runs; placement answers where, and the harness used to skip it — every dispatch became a Task subagent, in your pane, your context, your working tree. Inside herdr, building Stage 2 now places each one: a long gate or suite gets its own pane (same cwd, it only reads), parallel [P] editors and a fix in a vendor/ package get a worktree (a subagent cannot have a different checkout at all), everything else stays a subagent. Outside herdr placement does not exist and behaviour is unchanged. the vendored-package floor — Write/Edit inside vendor/ or node_modules/ now asks, naming why that edit neither survives nor ships (outside deploy.payload, overwritten by the next install) and, for a composer --prefer-source checkout, that the fix belongs in that package own repo. Edit reached NO floor before this: only Write and Bash were inspected. herdr-moments gains the three moments it was missing — a flow verb refusing on a dirty tree, a bug in an imported package, a long gate run. a lane-less tasks.md WARNs — the AC-2 silence is for legacy-waived artifacts only; planning: an older plan in the project is not the grammar. 0.21.1: the stop hook writes memory/ at the project root (walks up from a vendor-tree cwd, never writes under themes/plugins/vendor/packages). Netdust overlay on superpowers — superpowers is the process workhorse (brainstorm, plan, TDD, review, finish); netdust-agent adds the gates: an intake router (class A–F priced by open decisions + a stakes dial), plan-time gates machine-checked by bin/gate-check.py (threat model, invariants, ground-truth, Source: per FR, deliverable-first ordering, behaviour clusters), build-time gates (tier-based testing through the netdust WP harness, review clusters with independent reviewers, feature tests by an independent test-author after each task group), and a self-contained machine layer (hooks + bin/ scripts, bare python3) that verifies artifacts instead of trusting testimony. 0.21 (the inversion): a verification LANE per cluster — `Lane: behaviour` by default (one outside-observable RED for the cluster, bare tasks, no cluster panel, one branch review; the honest lane for CPTs, field maps and services over a framework that already carries the rule), `Lane: contract` by exception (today's per-task grammar), machine-refused only in the unsafe direction (a security-boundary path, high stakes); a model ladder per dispatch kind × lane, measured by run-cost's per-model block; herdr moments (seam tab, worktree isolation, status tab, doorbell, branch-review pane) gated on HERDR_ENV. 0.18 (the re-thinning): 27 skills cut to 6 thin overlays that actually invoke their superpowers base; verify-budget is telemetry, never a HALT; skills ship with evals; and an on-demand convergence gate (/converge) — the codebase read against specs/<feature>/ for what was promised but never built, gaps appended to tasks.md as a PROPOSED phase behind gate-check + the seam.
